# Chapter 3 — Communication Compliance by Organizational Segment

::: {.callout-note}
## In this chapter
Communication Compliance policies supervise messages for regulated-conduct, harassment, or sensitive-information patterns, and they assign reviewers to act on matches. Which segments are supervised, against which classifiers, and by which reviewers, are organizational decisions. This chapter scopes Communication Compliance policies, their supervised-user populations, and their reviewer assignments through OrgPath — so supervision follows organizational position, reviewers are drawn from the right oversight chain, and the segregation between the supervised and their reviewers is structurally enforced.
:::

## What Communication Compliance Supervises, and the Org Questions Hidden In It

Frame the surface: supervised populations, classifiers/policies, and reviewer assignment. Surface the three organizational questions native configuration buries — who is supervised, who reviews them, and that the two sets must not overlap.

## Scoping Supervised Populations Through OrgPath

Mechanism for the supervised set: a reconciliation job reads OrgTree nodes flagged for Communication Compliance scope and maintains the policy's supervised-user membership by OrgPath, idempotently, with drift findings — the same explicit-driver pattern as IRM, since Communication Compliance also does not consume an Adaptive Policy Scope.

## Reviewer Assignment From the Organizational Oversight Chain

Develop the reviewer side: reviewers should be resolved from the segment's oversight chain in the OrgTree (a compliance or supervisory node), not hand-listed. Show how OrgPath makes the reviewer population a derived, maintainable set rather than a static configuration that rots.

## Structural Segregation of Duties Between Supervised and Reviewer

The integrity property: because both populations are derived from OrgPath, the reconciliation job can assert that the reviewer set and the supervised set are disjoint and emit a `DRIFT-SEGREGATION` finding when they are not — turning a manual audit check into a continuous structural invariant.

## Operational Cadence and the Privacy Boundary

Close on cadence and guardrails: supervision changes are sensitive, so the job is gated by the privacy review formalized in Chapter 6, and every change is evidence-logged. Note the GCC-Moderate considerations for classifier availability and reviewer tooling.
